_comment: Hand-written contextual items, for the levels the generator cannot serve. Read by scripts/content/build_level_test.mjs, which validates every one of them against exactly the rules it applies to the items it builds itself — a curated item that fails a frame rule is a build failure, not an exception. Written 2026-09-10, after the frame rules removed 174 items and took the beginner band's gap-fill exercise with them: only 15 of the taught words below level 6 kept an item, down from 50, and Today's Vocabulary and Review lost the mode almost entirely for a new learner. See docs/CONTENT_REMEDIATION_LEDGER.md C-008.
_rules: before + '____' + after is the rendered prompt. `answer` and `options` are word ids; the answer is not repeated in `options`. Every option must share the answer's category, sit within a few levels of it, agree with the particle the sentence carries — so the particle never gives the answer away — and be false in the finished sentence, which is a judgement and is recorded in `why`.

items.why: One waters a flower. Rice, food and soup are all consonant-final food nouns and none of them is given to a plant.
Milk, coffee and juice are liquids: nothing is grilled over a fire. All four are vowel-final, so 를 says nothing.
깎다 needs something with a skin. Milk, coffee and cooking have none. The verb of eating is deliberately absent: with it, every food would fit.
Four consonant-final body words, and only one of them sees. 발 is kept out because ㄹ takes 로 and the particle would give the answer away.
The same set, the other sense: singing is the mouth.
Four vowel-final body words. A nose, a head and a leg do not hear.
감다 in this sense is washing hair and nothing else — 귀를 감다 is not Korean.
Walking is the legs; hurting an ear or a nose does not make it hard.
손을 잡다 is what people do with a friend. One does not take a friend's eye, mouth or body.
입다 takes clothing. A door, a room and a desk are in the same drawer and none is worn.
신다 is only footwear — clothes are 입다, and a door and a desk are neither.
쓰다 on the head. Trousers go on the legs, a chair and a clock go nowhere on a person.
A bag holds things. A chair and a mirror do not, and a hat is not where a book goes.
Only a clock tells the time. All four are vowel-final, so 를 gives nothing away.
One combs one's hair in front of a mirror; a room, a toothbrush and a bathroom are not looked into.
닫다 takes a door. Clothes, a room and a desk are not closed on the way out of a classroom.
A library lends books. Words, music and a photograph are not borrowed from one.
찍다 is the verb for a photograph and for none of the others.
부르다 of a song. A telephone, a film and a chat are not sung.
부치다 is posting. A telephone, a film and a song do not go through the post.
Only one of the four is a place a child learns Hangul in.
내다 of money. A market, a convenience store and a bank are places — one does not hand a shop a bank.
